findings.reason: the node should extend or lift the existing predicate (and death_census.py, which owns terminal-shape classification) rather than fork a parallel detector.
findings.text: _session_too_large_to_continue already reads exactly §9's shape-5 predicate ("the run announced a compaction that never completed a boundary", reading system/status compacting against system/compact_boundary) and _dispatch_session at dispatch.py:11489 already withholds that session so recovery starts fresh; §9 instead proposes its own live classifier without naming that this owner exists, so one stream shape would acquire a second reader and a second notion of "too large to continue".

findings.reason: naming the fresh-session half as already complete leaves §9's prevention limited to the compaction threshold and bounded turns it actually still owes.
findings.text: §9 offers "a fresh session instead of an inherited one (§8)" as a prevention candidate, but §8 already landed this: session reuse is keyed to the run's own task and dispatch withholds a session whose prior run ended too large, so the candidate restates landed behaviour and the section never says why the existing gate cannot carry whatever is left.

findings.reason: a section that adds an interface family must account for it in its own text, and here the classification belongs in an owner that already classifies terminal shapes.
findings.text: §9 says dispatch should detect shape 5 "and end the run as its own classification" — a new terminal classification — without naming what in the existing vocabulary (the death_census completed/dead/running/unreadable set, or the D-numbered dispatch refusal families in reckon/crew/refusals.py) it retires, merges, or extends, while omnibus counts stand at public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23.

findings.reason: an implementation brief built from §9 as written would rebuild machinery the reader is never told exists.
findings.text: §9's prevention half proposes a compaction classifier and a fresh-session rule as if new, but cites neither _session_too… (dispatch.py:11289) nor the landed session-freshness gate (§8) that already implement both, so the node as written would search for prior art only after dispatch.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan extends existing owners (reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/doccheck.py, reckon/_plan_html.py) rather than introducing a new module, so there is no new interface to judge for depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §9 shape-5 prevention re-implements compaction-shape detection that reckon/crew/dispatch.py:11289 already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §9 adds a run classification without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the landed sections cite their prior art extensively (classify_pointer, record_process_alive, _review_lane_candidates, context_budget, effective_input_window), but §9's unlanded prevention half proposes a fresh-session and compaction classifier without citing the mechanism that already implements both.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §9's prevention candidate "a fresh session instead of an inherited one (§8)" adds no behaviour the already-landed dispatch session gate lacks.
